inputs.README.md:
# Pantry Map

A local command-line inventory summary for volunteer food cooperatives.

Current use: python3 pantry.py stock.csv. The CSV has item, quantity, location columns. The program prints totals by item as JSON. Volunteers maintain the CSV themselves.

The cooperative wants a long-term direction: help volunteers prevent food waste and reliably share stock between sites while keeping local operation possible. No cloud vendor or commercial model has been chosen.

# Pantry Map: Vision and Technical Horizons

Owner: Pantry Map cooperative stewards
Status: proposed vision
Last verified: 2026-10-28

## A dependable shared pantry

Pantry Map should let volunteer cooperatives turn food that would be wasted into food people can use. A volunteer should know what is physically present, what needs using soon, what another site can actually promise, and who will complete a handover. Each cooperative must remain able to receive, distribute and reconcile food when its internet connection, a partner site or a hosting provider is unavailable.

The ambition is a network of locally governed pantries that can coordinate reliable transfers without surrendering their records or depending on a central operator. Success means less edible food discarded and fewer fruitless journeys, achieved with volunteer effort a small cooperative can sustain. More transactions or a more elaborate system do not establish success.

Consider a volunteer receiving surplus vegetables at North. They record the lot, quantity, unit and handling deadline locally. South can accept part of it and has a volunteer who can collect. North confirms a specific allocation; both sites can see its age and status. During an outage, South can still distribute its own stock. A delayed acceptance does not silently become a promise: the sites resolve uncertain transfers by phone or in person, then reconcile the record. The receiving volunteer confirms the actual amount and condition. A coordinator sees the remaining food needing attention and an intelligible history of differences. Humans judge suitability, dietary needs, equitable allocation and whether a journey is worthwhile. Pantry Map supplies evidence and coordination; it does not certify food safety or decide who deserves food.

Local operation and understandable records are durable principles. The present practice of maintaining a CSV by hand is a useful starting contract, not an eternal interface constraint. No commercial model, cloud vendor, calendar deadline or autonomous decision maker is assumed. Cooperative consent, connectivity, device availability and training capacity remain strategic inputs to test.

## What exists today

[README.md](README.md) describes a local command-line summary and manually maintained `item,quantity,location` CSV. [pantry.py](pantry.py) reads that CSV, converts quantity to an integer and adds quantities by item. The executable smoke check `python3 pantry.py stock.csv` returned `{"beans": 6, "rice": 15}` on 2026-10-28. The example [stock.csv](stock.csv) contains rice at two locations; the summary combines those locations. The code offers no lot or unit model, expiry tracking, durable edit history, reservation, transfer coordination, authentication, synchronization or recovery mechanism. Malformed or missing inputs are not handled as volunteer-facing errors. This is a verified tiny baseline, not evidence of a deployed multi-site service.

Target-scoped MCP/index retrieval is unavailable in this fixture; evidence comes from targeted local reads and this one safe smoke check. No volunteer observation or production outcome data was supplied. Everything below is proposed engineering or explicitly named research, not shipped capability. The manual CSV workflow can remain available for migration and export while a new operational store is explored.

## Foundations and ownership

The proposed system separates what a site knows from what the network has heard. Each site owns its inventory and allocations. A local durable store records receipts, corrections, distribution and transfer events, with stable IDs, explicit units, lot identity, provenance and an audit trail. The stock view is derived from those records; imports are staged and reconciled rather than overwriting trusted state. A small local application provides understandable forms, searches and printable/exportable views. A phone or paper fallback remains an operational procedure.

Between sites, versioned messages carry offers, reservation requests, source confirmations, dispatches, receipts and cancellations. The source site is authoritative for allocating its own stock. Every local distribution and allocation must share an atomic availability check that respects outstanding commitments. A count correction that invalidates a commitment creates a visible exception rather than silently cancelling or fulfilling the promise. A receiver's cached availability is an observation with a timestamp, never permission to spend stock. Offline cross-site requests remain tentative until the source confirms. Duplicate and delayed messages must be harmless, acknowledgements explicit, and contradictory states visible for human resolution. A relay may help delivery but is replaceable; a relay does not own inventory. Direct exchange, removable exports and a hosted relay are options to compare, not decisions already made.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  V[Volunteer] --> A[Proposed local application]
  A --> L[Proposed site-owned durable records]
  L --> S[Stock and deadline views]
  L --> X[Versioned exchange adapter]
  X <-->|Untrusted delayed messages| R[Optional replaceable relay or direct exchange]
  R <--> P[Partner site and its own records]
```

All diagram components are proposed. The existing CLI remains a separate import/export compatibility path until migration is demonstrated. Trust boundaries are volunteer/device access, imported files and partner messages. Proposed controls include site identity, role-limited corrections and allocations, validated message schemas, authenticated exchange, minimal shared personal data, and key revocation/recovery. These need specialist design before implementation; this vision provides no security approval. Keep beneficiary names out of network inventory messages unless a separately justified, consented use requires them. Backup, restore, schema migration and exit exports belong to the first durable store, not a later polish phase.

The unresolved offline boundary is deliberate: local distribution can continue while disconnected, but global instantaneous allocation cannot be guaranteed across independent disconnected writers. Start with one allocating authority per site; disconnected secondary devices queue observations or requests. Multi-device offline write authority is a separate research decision. Failure to find an operable authority model would limit the network ambition, not justify hidden overbooking.

## Capability horizons

These are thresholds in useful behavior, not dates. Every numerical exit below is a proposed pilot target to agree with participating cooperatives before a trial; none is a measured result. An evaluator who did not build the capability must collect evidence and may reject a threshold.

### 1. A local record volunteers can trust

A volunteer can receive a lot, correct a mistake, see stock by site and unit, record distribution, and identify food nearing its handling deadline without internet. Foundations are a validated lot/unit schema, explicit corrections, a durable local event history, accessible input and stock views, import/export contracts, and tested backup/restore. Record entry time, reconciliation discrepancies, rejected inputs and recovery failures. Prerequisites are observing actual receiving/distribution work and agreeing what “quantity,” “usable” and a deadline mean; the present integer totals cannot answer those questions.

Demonstration: two volunteers receive and distribute mixed units, import a CSV with a bad row, correct a count, lose a device copy and restore from backup while disconnected. The unchanged CLI fails because it has no edits, lots, deadline view or recovery history. A cooperative steward independent of implementation checks all 30 scripted stock movements against physical counts and requires zero unexplained differences or silent invalid rows, complete correction attribution, a successful restore, and at least 90% of ten representative tasks completed without developer rescue. Observe two operating weeks; record all rescues and abandoned tasks. Fail if the record looks correct while food has vanished, corrections destroy history, or maintenance exceeds a volunteer's agreed weekly budget. The uncertain bet is that better records repay entry effort; stop adding features if they do not. This horizon is useful as a single-site tool even if networking never arrives, and supplies the stable identities and corrections required for exchange.

### 2. A handover that becomes a fulfilled promise

Two sites can make and complete a specific transfer with intelligible exceptions. Build offers tied to lots, source-authorized allocations, reservation/dispatch/receipt state transitions, partial quantities, cancellation, expiry and reconciliation. Define which actor can advance each state and when a held amount is released. Begin with supervised exchange or a deliberately simple local export/import adapter, before solving automated delivery. Instrument stale offers, allocation conflicts, unacknowledged handovers, quantity differences and time to resolve them. Prerequisites are horizon 1 records and agreement on collection responsibilities and exception contacts.

Demonstration: North offers food, South requests it, North confirms, a second request and a local distribution compete for the same stock, only part is collected and the receiver reports a discrepancy. A site steward verifies 20 scripted transfers including duplicate requests, cancellation and expired offers, with no source allocation beyond usable stock and every item accounted for as retained, reserved, dispatched, received or explicitly unresolved. A transfer coordinator who did not build it then compares four weeks of real handovers with deadline-list plus phone coordination. Before the trial, cooperatives agree meaningful minimum floors for on-time fulfilled handovers and promised quantity actually received, using observed current practice; advancement requires meeting both floors without degrading fulfillment against the comparator. Separately, at least 95% of exceptions must be explicitly resolved within the agreed operating window, with zero undisclosed failed collections. Count cancellations, partial receipts and phone rescues separately; a resolved cancellation is not a fulfilled promise. Baseline CSV totals cannot represent a promise or its fulfillment. Fail if reservations strand food past usability, uncertain transfers look complete, or staff resolve discrepancies by deleting evidence. The research question is whether the reservation burden prevents more failed journeys than it causes. A successful two-site manual exchange is already valuable even if a larger network is unjustified; it establishes the protocol that automated transport must preserve.

### 3. Cooperative exchange through interruption

Several sites coordinate while each keeps operating independently. Implement an outbox/inbox (remember unsent and received messages), idempotent handling (repeats have no extra effect), version negotiation (detect incompatible partner message formats), durable acknowledgements, stale-state display and an exception queue. Choose transport by comparing direct exchange and an optional relay against actual connectivity and support cost. Sites retain authoritative records, export formats and a tested path to replace the relay. An offline request cannot reserve remote food; the UI must show tentative versus source-confirmed state. Prerequisites are the proven transfer protocol, partner identity/revocation design and agreed data-sharing governance.

Demonstration: three sites exchange messages that are reordered, duplicated or unavailable for 48 hours, revoke one partner, restore a site from an older backup missing acknowledged transfers, and resume coordination. Restored stock cannot support new allocations or distributions until prior confirmed or dispatched transfers have been recovered or explicitly reconciled; affected lots may need a temporary pause. No confirmed allocation is created twice, no unconfirmed request is presented as a promise, local distributions continue, and every unresolved discrepancy is visible. An independent reliability tester checks all scripted transitions and a cooperative steward witnesses relay replacement using exported records. A replacement steward then inherits recovery authority, operating instructions and unresolved transfers without the predecessor, and completes one routine operating cycle; record any rescue or authority gap. In a six-week pilot require recovery without developer intervention in at least 90% of rehearsed incidents, no unexplained stock loss, and no more than the support time budget agreed before trial. Baseline CSV has no message or reconciliation behavior and fails this demonstration. Fail if reconnecting corrupts local truth, revoked credentials retain unintended access, or only the original developer can recover the network. Useful intermediate value is resilient coordination for a small federation; it does not depend on prediction or nationwide scale. The open research is the cost and safety of identity recovery and multiple disconnected devices; further expansion waits on evidence.

### 4. Waste prevention as a cooperative capability

The network helps volunteers see preventable waste early, assemble feasible transfer options and learn which interventions actually help. Build explainable deadline views, consented aggregate outcome reports, capacity/transport constraints and optional suggestions based on observed demand. Suggestion ranking, forecasting and route optimization are research bets; compare them with simple deadline ordering and a shared call list before investing. Humans accept transfers and manage food suitability; no recommendation commits stock. Prerequisites are trustworthy operational history, meaningful waste/distribution categories and enough representative observations to evaluate them.

Demonstration: during a seasonal surplus and transport disruption, sites identify edible at-risk food, arrange human-approved transfers and distribute it before its handling deadline, then show both prevented waste and the effort spent. An evaluator selected jointly by cooperatives compares at least eight weeks before and eight after, using a matched site or staggered rollout where feasible; adjust for donations, food mix, closures and seasonality and state causal limits. Proposed success targets are 20% lower edible discard per unit received, no increase in missed confirmed collections, and no increase in median weekly administrative time. Report uncertainty and reject claims unsupported by sample size. CSV totals fail because they cannot connect lots, deadlines, interventions and outcomes. Fail if food is merely moved before being discarded elsewhere, recipient access worsens, or improved reporting is mistaken for improved outcomes. Even a negative forecasting result is valuable if simple deadline coordination works; advanced prediction is optional, reliable cooperation is not.

## Investment, evaluation and decisions

The critical path is understanding volunteer work → trustworthy local state → accountable promises → resilient exchange → demonstrated prevention. Accessibility trials, governance interviews and transport experiments can run alongside schema work; federation cannot repair unreliable stock, and prediction cannot repair missing outcomes. Expand participants only after the previous threshold is independently witnessed. More specialists would buy parallel field studies, recovery experiments and alternative transport prototypes, not remove physical counting, volunteer consent or seasonal observation bottlenecks. No resource assumption is supplied and no fixed completion date is promised.

Across pilots, establish baseline discard, unfulfilled confirmed transfers, count discrepancies, time spent entering and repairing records, training time, support hours and full device/hosting/backup costs. Use agreed units by food category rather than adding kilograms to item counts. Include low-connectivity sites, first-time and returning volunteers, mixed units, partial handovers, damaged stock and personnel turnover. Count failures, abandonment, paper/phone rescues and later regressions. Recheck four weeks after a pilot ends to see whether volunteers still use and maintain it. Publish results back to participating cooperatives in plain language; no live data publication is authorized by this vision. An implementation team cannot grade its own outcome claim alone.

The most fragile assumptions are that volunteers will record events in time; that source-controlled allocation fits real cooperative practice; that shared availability produces feasible transport rather than more work; and that sites can sustain recovery and stewardship. The cheapest meaningful next investment is a bounded field investigation at two willing sites: observe one receiving/distribution cycle, replay ten recent handovers on paper, agree quantity/deadline vocabulary and support budgets, and compare a deadline list plus phone coordination against current practice. Deliver an evidence-backed schema and a go/no-go recommendation for horizon 1, not a federation build. Open operator decisions include participating sites, acceptable data sharing, identity and authoritative-state recovery authority, accessibility/language needs, transport responsibilities and acceptable support cost.

The ultimate demonstration is an independently witnessed surplus season in which participating cooperatives prevent measurable edible waste, fulfill accepted handovers and recover through a prolonged connectivity loss, while a newly trained volunteer can inspect, restore and leave the system with usable records. The destination is durable cooperative capability, supported by software that earns its upkeep.

## Review record

D1, reviewed on 2026-10-28, SHA256 `380fa35b898f916a8fc8bd457b5d917965d9e18a51155a7ebd95bb914842465e`. All initial workers read this same frozen draft and the target brief; local source evidence was available. The author performed one bounded repair pass to produce D2. These are advisory artifact reviews, with no lifecycle approval or implementation authority.

- Architecture: independent worker `/root/envision_trial/architecture`, advisory support with ARCH-01 and ARCH-02 clarifications. Repairs add atomic stock consumption across distribution and allocation, visible exceptions when corrections invalidate promises, and an older-backup recovery demonstration that reconciles prior obligations before using restored stock.
- Standalone red-team: independent worker `/root/envision_trial/redteam`, `feature-definition-challenge`, all five thinking stances. RT-01 found that documented cancellations could satisfy the handover exit criterion. The repair separates real fulfillment and received quantities from exception resolution, requires agreed fulfillment floors and a phone-coordination comparison, and counts cancellations, partial receipts and rescues.
- Archetype Council: independent chair `/root/envision_trial/council_chair`, canonical five seats with no swap, optional primer skipped. Fresh isolated seat contexts were instructed to declare axes before reading: Sun Tzu (strategic positioning), Yoda (reader readiness), Spock (testable claims), Marcus Aurelius (durability/control), Feynman (simplicity). Seats received no other seat findings or the standalone red-team output before judging. All individual seat verdicts were `ready`; the initial aggregate was held `NOT READY` pending the acceptance-criterion repair. Spock independently reproduced RT-01 as SP-1; Marcus MA-1 sharpened succession testing; Feynman F-1 requested short messaging-term explanations. The red-team closing pass held SP-1 and F-1, narrowed MA-1 to inherited authority and obligations, and introduced no new findings.

| Finding | Disposition | Incorporated change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ARCH-01 | do_now | Shared atomic availability invariant and competing local distribution demonstration. |
| ARCH-02 | do_now | Restore acknowledged obligations before stock is reused; recovery authority remains a design decision. |
| RT-01 / SP-1 | do_now | Separate fulfillment from resolution and compare actual handovers with simple coordination. |
| MA-1 | maybe_later | Completed in the bounded repair: a successor steward inherits authority and obligations without the predecessor. |
| F-1 | maybe_later | Completed in the bounded repair: inline explanations of three messaging concepts. |

`maybe_later` here means optional improvement worth completing now, not deferred work. Independent focused verification of D2 (`cc158e2d1966fc7f8c4b83d1b6b93a8c9d4f6382b9303ec0ea9ad78721435008`) closed ARCH-01/02 and RT-01/SP-1; the chair and red-team also confirmed MA-1/F-1. No actionable finding remains within this bounded review scope. **Archetype Council — PASS WITH IN-SESSION FIXES** (independent chair; all five canonical seats; strongest axis: Spock; one moderator-derived required repair and two advisory improvements completed). Five axes were exercised, with partial overlap between strategic positioning and simplicity. The strongest alternative is deadline-list plus phone coordination; it remains the comparison that the proposed workflow must earn its place against.

### Falsification Check

The working verdict is PASS WITH IN-SESSION FIXES. The strongest opposing argument is that orderly exception handling can coexist with failed food delivery. It does not overturn this document verdict: D2 separates physical fulfillment floors and comparator outcomes from exception closure. Whether the system achieves those outcomes remains unproven and belongs to the pilots.

Review provenance: the five isolated workers were `/root/envision_trial/council_chair/{sun_tzu,yoda,spock,marcus,feynman}`. Three final outputs retained explicit axis declarations; Sun Tzu and Yoda subsequently attested from retained context that declarations preceded their first tool call. The coordinator could not independently inspect that original commentary timing. Sun Tzu's original explicit null finding omitted the protocol's exact null phrase, which was confirmed afterward without rereading or rerunning the review. These process evidence limits are retained rather than represented as mechanically verified protocol compliance. Architecture, red-team and chair performed focused verification in their existing independent reviewer contexts; the author alone made repairs. No automatic second repair cycle ran.

Strategic uncertainty remains about volunteer entry burden, transport value, recovery governance and affordable support. No field trial or future capability has been verified; no security specialist review was performed. Target-scoped MCP and a supported documentation checker are unavailable; local checks confirmed all three citation targets, the four ordered horizon sections and the corrected outcome criterion. Manual review checked prerequisites and each horizon’s content; these checks do not establish operational capability.

thinking_stances_applied:
- Adversarial: a pilot could cancel every confirmed transfer, record each cancellation correctly, and satisfy the “fulfilled or explicitly resolved” threshold.
- Constructive: separate reconciliation completeness from actual handover reliability.
- Simplicity: retain the proposed deadline-list/phone comparison as the practical competing intervention.

strongest_challenge:
- RT-01 — Resolution can masquerade as reliable sharing. Evidence: horizon 2 allows at least 95% of confirmed handovers to end “fulfilled or explicitly resolved.” Inference: all transfers could fail yet satisfy that numerical target if their failures are documented. The wider vision clearly wants fulfilled promises, but this advancement criterion does not enforce that outcome.
- Paired fix: measure two separate outcomes: timely resolution of all exceptions, and actual fulfillment of confirmed transfers. Agree a fulfillment floor against current practice before the pilot; count cancellations, partial receipts and phone rescues explicitly.

best_alternative:
Keep the staged local-first vision, but make the two-site pilot an outcome comparison: deadline list plus phone coordination versus proposed transfer records. Track promised quantities, quantities received within the agreed window, failed journeys, cancellation reasons and volunteer time. Require independent evidence that the proposed workflow maintains or improves fulfillment while making exceptions accountable. This would be better because transparent failure remains valuable without being counted as successful sharing. Cost: additional observation and a potentially slower expansion decision.

consequence_of_current_path:
An orderly exception ledger could qualify the project for federation even when accepted promises rarely deliver food. Later automation would reproduce a workflow whose operational value remains unproven.

recommendation:
Amend horizon 2’s advancement criterion before accepting D1; retain its exception-resolution target as a separate measure.
